title: Amp Z data center (former Southland/Abitibi paper mill)
applicant: Amp Z Champion Data Center Holdings LLC; land owned by Verdant Industries LLC and Verdant Industries Realty LLC
bottom_line:
Hwy 103 East near Herty, just outside Lufkin.

Land: Verdant Industries and Verdant Industries Realty, which bought the mill from Abitibi in 2010 and 2012, granted Amp Z an option on about 1,041 acres (Lufkin Daily News). Corporate records name Eric Estes as Verdant's president; his late father, Harold Estes, managed it from 2014 until his death in 2025 (Lufkin Daily News, Sept. 18, 2026).

Power: Verdant holds a January 2025 state air authorization for 12 natural gas turbines. TCEQ asked whether the emissions could be lowered enough to avoid a more extensive federal review (Lufkin Daily News). Full build planned at 2.1 GW.

Water: The public was told about 500 gallons a day. The county abatement application lists water needs as "TBD," and city leaders said on record they won't cap water use. The city owns the mill's wells (bought 2009), and Pineywoods GCD says Amp Z has filed no well permits. Separately, Verdant is renewing the old mill's wastewater permit, which allows discharges averaging up to 5 million gallons a day into Paper Mill Creek, the Angelina River and Sam Rayburn Reservoir.

Taxes: The county rejected Amp Z's 10-year tax abatement request (Lufkin Daily News). In 2026 the appraisal district added about $1.8 million in value for existing buildings on two tracts, while most of the land stays taxed at timber value (Angelina CAD property IDs 120149, 29802, 28701).

Location approximate.

title: HyperDataGrid data center, Ben Dunn Road
bottom_line: Ben Dunn Road off Hwy 103 West, Angelina County. The developer told the groundwater district it would use about 500 gallons a day, then asked for a combined 13 million gallons a year, just under the 15-million-gallon line that would require a public hearing for all five wells on the property. Three are old sawmill wells whose permits (A0046-A0048, held by Temple-Inland) expired in 2018; the District says the other two were drilled to supply gas-well rigs and are not licensed for the landowner's use. As of Sept. 29, 2026, the District had taken no action. Source: Pineywoods GCD emails, Aug.-Sept. 2026. Location approximate; exact site not yet mapped.

title: Longleaf Power Station (WattBridge), north of Lufkin
applicant: Long Leaf Generating LLC / WattBridge Texas Holdings, LLC
bottom_line:
A 600 MW natural gas peaking plant in ERCOT's interconnection queue (project 26INR0294), connecting at the Redland Substation near Kurth Lake, north of Lufkin.

Tax break: Angelina County approved a 10-year tax abatement for Long Leaf Generating LLC in May 2025: 100% for the first three years, then stepping down. The company must invest at least $350 million and create nine full-time jobs, and the county attorney said it must operate as a peaking plant, supplying power when demand is high (Lufkin Daily News).

Water: Approved for 80 million gallons a year in late 2024 or early 2025 (never drilled). In March 2026 it switched to 24/7 operation and requested 1.5 billion gallons a year, about 4.1 million gallons a day. On hold since July 2026 at the company's request. Source: Pineywoods GCD general manager. A 24/7 plant is not a peaking plant, so this change may conflict with the abatement terms.

Location approximate, near Kurth Lake.
